original_question: Determine the order of the first conjugate point along any L2 geodesic in D_mu^s(M) starting at the identity, and decide whether the existence of conjugate points is related to Arnold's stability criterion for stationary flows.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 19(a)-(b) ("More differential geometry: the L^2 exponential map and its singularities").
correct_elements: It already captures both parts of the exact target in the paper: (i) determining the order of the first conjugate point along an L^2 geodesic issuing from the identity in D^s_μ(M), and (ii) asking whether conjugate points are related to Arnold's stability criterion for stationary flows.
missing_details: The paper's question is explicitly about 2D hydrodynamics, not arbitrary dimension.
M should be specified as a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary.
D^s_μ(M) is the Sobolev H^s completion of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group D_μ(M).
The regularity condition s > n/2 + 1 is part of the setup; in the 2D case this means s > 2.
The geodesics are geodesics of Arnold's right-invariant kinetic-energy L^2 metric, not geodesics for an unspecified metric.

The quantifier is universal: the question is about every geodesic γ(t)=exp_e(tv_0) issuing from the identity e, with v_0 in T_eD^s_μ(M) (equivalently, a sufficiently regular divergence-free vector field, tangent to the boundary when there is one).

The 'first conjugate point' is meant as the first conjugate point of the L^2 exponential map along the geodesic ray from e; the surrounding context distinguishes mono-conjugate and epi-conjugate points in infinite dimensions, so the intended notion of 'order' is the multiplicity/order of that conjugate point.
Arnold's stability criterion should be spelled out as positive or negative definiteness of the second variation of the kinetic energy restricted to coadjoint orbits.

For part (b), the paper's nearby evidence is specifically that on the disk, annulus, and straight channel, steady flows satisfying Arnold's stability criterion have no conjugate points; in that discussion the authors assume the 2D domain has nonempty boundary.
refined_question: For a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M, possibly with boundary, fix s > 2 and let D^s_μ(M) be the H^s Sobolev completion of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group, endowed with Arnold's right-invariant kinetic-energy L^2 metric and exponential map exp_e. Given any geodesic γ(t)=exp_e(tv_0) issuing from the identity e, where v_0 is a divergence-free H^s vector field tangent to ∂M when ∂M is nonempty, determine the order (multiplicity) of the first conjugate point of exp_e along γ. Further, determine whether the existence of conjugate points in D^s_μ(M) is related to Arnold's stability criterion for stationary Euler flows on M, namely positive or negative definiteness of the second variation of the kinetic energy restricted to coadjoint orbits.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's exact formulation: it is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 19(a)-(b) in Section 7. To make it stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the paper's setup from Section 1 and Section 5.2: the right-invariant kinetic-energy L^2 metric on D_μ(M), the Sobolev completion D^s_μ(M), the regularity condition s > n/2 + 1, and the exponential map exp_e(tv_0)=γ(t). The nearby context in Section 7 also matters: Theorem 7.1 explains why the problem is posed in 2D by giving the Fredholm index-zero property there, and the paragraph immediately after Problem 19 defines Arnold's criterion and records the known simple-domain evidence motivating part (b).
